resources.string: Scan, signal, band, link and ping
From Android 13 Wi-Fi scans also need the \"nearby Wi-Fi devices\" permission.
Location is off: no scan results
%1$d networks: %2$d at 2.4 GHz, %3$d at 5 GHz, %4$d at 6 GHz
No Wi-Fi feature, service or wlan interface: nothing to test.
FEATURE_WIFI is missing: android.hardware.wifi.xml is not installed in vendor/etc/permissions, so apps that require Wi-Fi are hidden from the store even if the radio works.
The device declares Wi-Fi but WifiManager is not available: the Wi-Fi service did not start (system_server log, wifi APEX).

The framework says Wi-Fi is on but the kernel has no network interface with that name: the driver did not create it (wlan.ko not loaded, firmware download failed) or wifi.interface points to the wrong name.

Turn Wi-Fi on and run again. If the switch turns itself off after a few seconds, the driver or firmware failed to load: look for wlan, cnss or wcnss in dmesg and for WifiHal/wificond errors in logcat.
Wi-Fi did not reach ENABLED within 6 s. A hang here is usually the driver load or the firmware download (wlan.ko, WCNSS/cnss firmware, board data), or a vendor Wi-Fi HAL that never answers.
WifiManager reports an unknown state: the Wi-Fi HAL or supplicant is in an error state. Check logcat for WifiVendorHal and wpa_supplicant.
Wi-Fi is on but no band is reported. Bands come from the vendor HAL and wificond (getSupportedBands); empty bands mean the HAL did not answer or is too old for this framework.
Band support is only known after Wi-Fi has been turned on once.
The HAL reports no Wi-Fi standards. Common with legacy vendor HALs and not a fault by itself.
Connect to an access point to test signal, IP configuration and internet access.
Connect to an access point first.
RSSI %1$d dBm is not a real signal value: the driver does not report station info (nl80211 get_station) or the vendor HAL link-layer stats.
Connected without a frequency: the driver does not report the operating channel.
Connected but the link rate is unknown: the driver does not report the bitrate (station info TX/RX rate).
Connected on %1$s although the framework says that band is not supported: the capability list from the HAL is wrong or stale.
/proc/net/wireless says %1$d dBm but the framework says %2$d dBm: one of the two is not updated by the driver.
Weak signal (%1$d dBm). Move closer to the access point; if it stays weak right next to it, check the antenna path or the board data file (bdwlan) used for calibration.
Associated but ConnectivityService has no network yet: DHCP is still running or failed. Wait a few seconds and run again.

Associated without IPv4 or global IPv6: DHCP failed. With a working access point this points at the data path (keys not installed after the 4-way handshake, firmware dropping frames) or at SELinux denials for the network stack.
No default route on Wi-Fi: DHCP gave no router, or the route was not installed.
No DNS server on Wi-Fi: names will not resolve unless Private DNS is set.
The interface address is not readable by apps on this ROM (SELinux). Not a fault.
The interface has no MAC address: the MAC is not provisioned (wlan_mac.bin, NV item or device tree) and the driver did not generate one.

00:03:7F is the default address of Qualcomm Atheros board data: the real MAC is not provisioned (wlan_mac.bin in persist or the NV item read by cnss-daemon). Every phone running this ROM gets the same address.
The interface uses a locally administered address: Android randomises the MAC per network by default, so the factory MAC cannot be seen while connected. Not a fault.
The interface uses a locally administered address while idle. If it changes at every boot even with randomisation off, the factory MAC is not provisioned and the driver makes one up.
Globally unique address with a vendor OUI. With MAC randomisation off this is the factory MAC.
Service %1$s is restarting: it crashes in a loop. Look at logcat and the tombstones for that service.
The driver could not be identified from sysfs; it may be hidden by SELinux.
Android returns no Wi-Fi scan results to apps while Location is off. Turn Location on and run again.

Wi-Fi is on and the scan completed, but not a single network was found. Unless the phone is in a shielded room this is a radio problem: firmware or board data (bdwlan), regulatory domain/country code blocking every channel, or a disconnected antenna.
No scan could be started (throttled or refused) and no cached results exist: the firmware may not be scanning at all. Wait two minutes and run again.
Every network has the same level (%1$d dBm): the driver reports a fixed value instead of the measured signal.
Some results have impossible levels (0 dBm or above, or below -110 dBm): the driver reports RSSI in the wrong unit or sign.
Android throttled the scan and the cached results are %1$d s old. The framework should rescan on its own while the screen is on: very old results suggest scans are failing.
Android throttles app scans (4 every 2 minutes); results from %1$d s ago were used. Developer options → \"Wi-Fi scan throttling\" can turn the limit off.
5 GHz is supported but no 5 GHz network was found while there are many at 2.4 GHz. If 5 GHz access points are nearby, the regulatory domain or country code may block those channels.
The ROM does not let apps send ICMP echo (net.ipv4.ping_group_range or SELinux). Not a Wi-Fi fault; the HTTP probe still tests the link.
The router does not answer ping. Some routers drop ICMP: if DNS and the internet probe below also fail, the link carries no traffic (keys not installed, firmware data path).
Packet loss towards the router on the local network. With a good signal this points at the firmware data path or power save; compare with another phone on the same access point.
Round trip to the router above 100 ms on the local network: often aggressive power save (PS-Poll) in the driver.
The ping host cannot be resolved: DNS does not work. Check the DNS servers above.
No reply from the internet host. The access point may be offline, or the host blocks ICMP: see the HTTP probe.
Packet loss towards the internet host. Compare with the gateway ping: loss only here comes from the internet line, not the phone.
Name resolution through the Wi-Fi network failed: no DNS server, an offline access point, or DNS blocked by the network.
The HTTP probe through Wi-Fi failed. If the gateway answers, the phone works and the problem is upstream (offline line, firewall). If nothing answers, the link carries no traffic.
The probe was redirected: this network has a captive portal (hotel, café). Log in with the browser and run again.
The probe URL answered with an unexpected status. Check the URL in Settings.
The download did not complete: %1$s. Offline networks and blocked URLs give this too; check the internet probe.
Below 1 Mbit/s. If the internet line is faster and the signal is good, suspect the firmware data path (aggregation, power save) or a CPU stuck at low frequency.
Signal and link rate, updated every second
Not connected (supplicant: %1$s). Connect to a network to see the live link.
Band, channel, width, standard and signal
Grant the location and nearby devices permissions above to see the networks.
Location is off: Android hides scan results until you turn it on.
Scan throttled by Android: showing results from %1$d s ago.
Stops after 15 s or 100 MB. The result also depends on the internet line: compare with another phone on the same access point. The URL can be changed in Settings.
Open a few web pages and a video in the browser while on Wi-Fi, then come back here.
Does the phone connect and browse normally, without drops or stalls?
